Which mode is right for you?
⚡
Quick Start — 3 minutes
You want a rough sanity check. Am I saving enough to retire at 60? You know your salary, SIP, and EPF. You have 3 minutes.
Best for: First-timers  ·  Quick check before a CA meeting  ·  Anyone who wants a number fast
You get: Readiness score · Corpus at retirement · Earliest retirement age · Top 3 risks · 3 specific actions this month
MOST USED
📋
Full Plan — 15 minutes
You want a real plan. Both incomes, all investments, parents, children goals, insurance check, tax comparison. Your actual retirement plan, not a rough estimate.
Best for: Families aged 35-55  ·  Anyone with parents to support  ·  Home loan + kids goals
You get: Year-by-year corpus table · Tax regime comparison · Insurance check · Family cashflow · Property LTCG · Children goals · What-if sliders · Parent support timeline · Withdrawal sequencing · Formula transparency · Downloadable PDF
🔧
Stress Test — 30 minutes
You are 2-5 years from retirement. Test every scenario before making irreversible decisions. RSU vesting, 1,000 market scenarios, CGT, SWP, portfolio rebalancing.
Best for: Retiring in the next 5 years  ·  RSUs or complex portfolio  ·  When the stakes are high
You get: 1,000 Monte Carlo scenarios · Health corpus buffer · Optimal SWP · CGT on each asset · LTCG on property · RSU vesting dashboard · Portfolio rebalancing in ₹ · Glide path · Downloadable PDF

Portfolio Health
Fill your investments to analyse
What needs attention
Specific rebalancing actions
What does my employer give me at retirement?
One-time payouts and recurring pension from your employer — with tax treatment applied.
What are my RSUs worth?
Your RSU vesting schedule, post-tax value, and how unvested RSUs are projected to grow. Taxes at vesting (perquisite) are deducted automatically.
What tax will I pay when I sell?
LTCG (10% above ₹1.25L) on equity MF & stocks. Post-tax corpus is what you actually keep.
Am I covered for medical costs?
Medical costs inflate at ~12% — far faster than general inflation. This is the dedicated buffer you need separate from your retirement corpus.
Should I prepay my loan or invest?
Uses your Loan 1 data & surplus from Tools tab. Compares guaranteed interest savings vs potential investment growth.
How do I draw my retirement income?
Models month-by-month corpus depletion with your SWP settings. Configure in the Tools tab.
How likely is my plan to succeed?
Randomly varies market returns and inflation to show the probability your corpus outlives you. Configure volatility in Tools tab.
📐 How is everything calculated? ▼
Every number uses standard actuarial and investment formulas. Live values from your plan are shown for each.
How should my portfolio shift with age?
Recommended equity/debt mix by age — shift from growth to income as you approach retirement. Yellow outline = your current age.

Step 1 of 4
Methodology, Privacy & Disclaimer

How corpus is calculated

Each instrument is projected independently to retirement using time-value-of-money formulas, then summed to a gross corpus. Deductions (child goals, loan balance, emergency fund) are subtracted to get net corpus.

  • EPF: Current balance compounded at 8.25% p.a. + monthly contributions via SIP formula
  • PPF: Balance at 7.1% p.a. + yearly deposits as annuity, both compounded to retirement
  • NPS: 60% as lump sum in corpus, 40% converted to monthly annuity at declared rate
  • Mutual funds / SIP: Balance at expected MF return + SIP with optional annual step-up via growing annuity formula
  • Salary surplus: Monthly surplus × growing annuity at MF rate (salary growth proxy 30% of declared rate)
  • Property (if sold): Future value at property rate → LTCG deducted → net proceeds compounded to retirement

Post-retirement drawdown

Each year: opening corpus × (1 + post-retirement return) − annual expense (inflated at post-retirement inflation). Simulation runs until corpus reaches zero or age 120, whichever comes first.

Monte Carlo simulation

1,000 iterations. Each run draws equity returns from a normal distribution (mean = base scenario, σ = volatility setting). Success rate = percentage of runs where corpus survives to life expectancy.

LTCG tax (Budget 2024)

Properties acquired before July 23, 2024: 20% with indexation (CII 5% p.a.). Properties acquired after July 23, 2024: 12.5% without indexation. Equity MF/stocks: 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25L/yr.

Default rate assumptions

  • Equity / MF return: 12% p.a. (base scenario)
  • Debt / FD return: 7% p.a.
  • PPF rate: 7.1% p.a.
  • EPF rate: 8.25% p.a.
  • NPS equity return: 10% p.a.
  • Property appreciation: 7% p.a.
  • Gold appreciation: 10% p.a.
  • General inflation: 5% p.a.
  • Medical inflation: 12% p.a.
  • Post-retirement portfolio return: 8% p.a.
  • Conservative scenario: returns −2%, inflation +1%
  • Optimistic scenario: returns +2%, inflation −1%

Known approximations

  • Salary surplus step-up uses 30% of salary growth rate as a proxy for expense control — directional, not exact
  • Loan balance reduction uses EMI × months, not an amortisation schedule — slightly underestimates remaining balance for fresh loans
  • EPF interest uses annual compounding; actual EPF compounds on monthly running balance (difference ~0.4%)
  • Child education corpus discounted at equity rate — optimistic if kept in fixed income

Your data never leaves your device

Retire Mitra runs entirely in your browser. No data is sent to any server, no account is created, no cookies are stored beyond your saved plan (localStorage).

AI Advisor

When you use the AI Advisor, your plan data is sent to Anthropic's API using your own API key. Anthropic's data retention policies apply. No data is sent without your explicit action (clicking "Ask Claude").

What is stored locally

  • Your plan data (JSON) — only when you click Save
  • UI preferences (dark/light mode, tier collapse state)
  • AI conversation history — in sessionStorage, cleared on tab close

To delete all stored data: Settings → Clear all data, or clear browser localStorage for this page.

Educational tool — not financial advice

Retire Mitra is a retirement planning calculator for educational and informational purposes only. It is not a SEBI-registered investment advisor, and nothing produced by this tool constitutes financial advice, tax advice, or legal advice.

Projections are estimates

All corpus projections, withdrawal rate calculations, and scenario analyses are based on assumed rates of return and inflation. Actual market returns will differ. Past performance is no guarantee of future results.

Consult a qualified professional

Before making any financial decision — including changes to SIP, EPF, NPS, insurance, or property — consult a SEBI-registered investment advisor, a chartered accountant, or a certified financial planner.

No liability

The creators of Retire Mitra accept no liability for financial decisions made based on outputs from this tool. Use at your own discretion.

📖 How to Use Retire Mitra
🚀 Getting Started
Where do I begin?
Start with the 👤 Self tab on the left — enter your age, target retirement age, and monthly expenses. Results appear live on the right as you type. Then work through each tab left to right: Self → Income → Finance → Assets → Family → Goals → Tools.
Can I try it before entering my own data?
Yes — click 🎮 Try Demo on the welcome screen (reload the page to see it). A complete sample Indian family profile loads. Explore all the output cards, then click ✏️ Enter My Own Numbers to clear everything and start fresh.
Do I need to fill everything?
No. Fill what you have — the tool calculates with whatever you provide. A quick estimate needs just: current age, retirement age, monthly expenses, and your main investments (MF + EPF). Takes under 5 minutes. A complete plan takes 15–20 minutes.
Is my data safe?
100% private. Everything stays in your browser. No server, no login, no tracking. Close the tab and all data is gone — unless you click 💾 Save Data first. The AI advisor only sends data when you explicitly click "Ask".
💡 Tip: Use the Conservative / Base / Optimistic buttons in the header to stress-test your plan under different return assumptions.
👤 Self Tab
Current age / Retirement age
Your age today in completed years. Retirement age = when you plan to stop working. Every year earlier dramatically increases corpus needed.
60 is most common. Retiring at 55 vs 60 needs ~40% more corpus (5 fewer earning years + 5 more spending years).
Life expectancy
How many years to fund in retirement. Default 85 is conservative — plan for 90–95 to be safe. A healthy 60-year-old today has a 30% chance of living past 90.
Monthly expenses (₹)
Your actual monthly household spend today. Include: rent/maintenance, food, utilities, transport, lifestyle, parents support, insurance premiums.
Exclude: loan EMIs (enter in Goals tab), SIPs/investments (enter in Finance tab).
Use last 3 months' bank + card statement average for accuracy.
Post-ret expense / growth rate
Leave blank to auto-inflate current expenses to retirement. Override only if you know your retirement lifestyle will cost significantly less (e.g. no rent after paying off home). Growth rate default 5% — slower than working years since you spend less on commute, work clothes, children.
Part-time income after retirement
Consulting, teaching, freelance in the first 5–10 years of retirement. Even ₹25K/mo for 7 years reduces corpus draw by ₹21L. Enter 0 if you plan to fully stop working.
Insurance — what to fill
Term life: sum assured (cover amount, not premium). Minimum 10× annual income. Enter annual premium separately.
Health: sum insured of your policy (the hospital bill limit, not premium). Recommended ₹10L+ base + ₹50L super top-up.
Critical illness: lump-sum on cancer/heart attack diagnosis. Separate from health insurance.
Endowment/ULIP: if you have LIC plans still paying premiums — enter maturity value and years to maturity.
Term cover: Annual income ₹24L → minimum ₹2.4Cr cover.
Emergency fund
Cash kept separate from investments — not part of your retirement corpus. Rule: 6 months of monthly expenses in a savings account or liquid MF.
💰 Income Tab
Gross CTC vs Net Salary
Enter your Gross CTC (Cost to Company — on your offer letter or Form 16). The tool auto-calculates your net take-home after tax under both New and Old regimes and picks whichever saves you more.
If you prefer to skip CTC, enter 0 there and fill your net monthly salary directly below.
New vs Old tax regime
Click ⚡ Auto (Best) — the tool automatically picks the better option for you. You can force-switch to compare. The annual tax saving is shown in the Tax Comparison card on the right side.
Annual salary growth (%)
Expected annual increment — typically 8–12% for IT/tech, 6–10% for other sectors. This determines your salary corpus (incremental savings invested each year).
Bonus, freelance, business income
Enter annual bonus as a yearly amount. Freelance and business income as monthly amounts. All are invested as part of your surplus corpus.
Passive / dividend income
Monthly income from dividends, P2P interest, royalties etc. Entered here as current monthly amount — inflation-adjusted at retirement to reduce shortfall from corpus.
📈 Finance Tab
EPF balance
Current EPF account balance. Find it at epfindia.gov.in → Passbook or on your latest salary slip. Grows at 8.25% p.a. tax-free. Also enter VPF (voluntary PF) monthly contribution in the field below.
NPS balance
NPS Tier 1 balance — check on NPS portal (npstrust.org.in) or your CRA (KARVY/NSDL) app. At retirement: minimum 40% must buy an annuity (monthly income). The remaining 60% is tax-free lump sum. Set your annuity % below the NPS field.
Equity MF (lump sum) vs Monthly SIP
MF value: current total market value of all equity MF holdings — check on Zerodha/Groww/CAMS/MFCentral (NAV × units).
Monthly SIP: total SIP across all equity MFs per month.
₹10K Nifty50 + ₹15K Flexicap + ₹10K ELSS = ₹35K total SIP
SIP step-up % — why it matters so much
How much you increase your SIP each year. This is the single biggest lever in your plan.
₹40K SIP flat for 22yr = ₹4.8Cr corpus.
₹40K SIP with 10% annual step-up = ₹9.4Cr — nearly double.
MF expense ratio
Annual cost charged by your mutual fund. Deducted from your effective return every year.
• Direct plans: 0.1–0.5%
• Regular plans (via distributor): 1–2%
On ₹2Cr over 22 years: 1% vs 0.5% expense ratio = ₹38L difference.
RSU (Restricted Stock Units) — foreign currency
Set the currency dropdown (USD/GBP/EUR/SGD) for each grant. Enter the stock price in that currency — the exchange rate bar converts to ₹ automatically. Update the exchange rate from Google if needed ("USD to INR" → paste in the rate box).
Annuities section — 4 types
Already receiving: enter current monthly payout (LIC Jeevan Akshay etc.).
Deferred annuity: plan still accumulating — enter current corpus + growth rate + payout rate. Converts to monthly income at retirement.
Guaranteed income plan: fixed monthly income from a future date.
Buy annuity at retirement: how much corpus to convert to guaranteed monthly income at retirement.
₹50L at 6.5% → ₹27,083/month guaranteed for life.
Post-retirement org benefits
Employer payouts at retirement: gratuity (tax-free up to ₹20L), leave encashment (₹25L exempt), VRS, superannuation. These are added to your retirement corpus with correct tax treatment applied automatically.
Foreign investments (401k, US stocks)
Enter current value in ₹ equivalent. Use the exchange rate from the RSU section. These grow at equity rate.
🏠 Assets Tab
Gold — enter in grams, not rupees
Enter total weight in grams across all forms (jewellery + coins). The tool multiplies by today's gold rate (default ₹9,500/gram — update if needed).
1 tola = 11.66g. A necklace ≈ 20–30g. Check hallmark certificate for exact weight.
Property value
Enter current market value — what you'd get if you sold today. Not the purchase price or circle rate. Check PropTiger, 99acres, or ask a local broker for comparable sales.
Enter the outstanding home loan in the loan field — it's deducted automatically to give net property equity.
Are physical assets part of retirement corpus?
Physical assets (gold, property) are included in your Total Net Worth and Family Wealth Pool — shown in the right panel. They are not counted as deployable corpus since you'd need to sell them. This distinction is intentional and accurate.
👪 Family Tab
Navigating with Back / Next buttons
The nav bar below the tab row shows your current tab and progress. Use ← Back and Next → to move through all 7 tabs in order. The 7 dots fill up as you progress — you can also click any dot to jump directly to that tab.
Why enter parents details?
The tool checks if your parents are financially self-sufficient. If their income (pension + other) covers their expenses, they show ✅. If not, the tool calculates exactly how much corpus you need to set aside to support them. This is separate from your retirement corpus.
What to enter for parents
Pension: monthly pension from employer or government.
Other income: FD interest, rent, dividends.
Monthly expenses: their household spend including medical.
Assets: their financial assets (FD, MF, PPF) + property + gold — used to calculate inheritance.
Children income section (new)
Scroll to the bottom of the Family tab to enter your earning children — sons and daughters. Enter age, monthly income, employment type, EPF/PPF balance, MF/stocks, and their monthly contribution to household. This populates the Everyone's financial picture card in the right panel, showing the complete household financial picture.
Everyone's financial picture (right panel)
A card in the right panel (after the Parents detail card) shows every family member's full financial picture — income, savings, assets — in a 3-column grid. Each card shows everything entered for that person. Data appears automatically as you fill the Income and Family tabs.
Inheritance percentage
Your expected share of parents' estate. This is added to your Family Wealth Pool (shown on right panel). The tool discounts it to present value correctly.
⚠️ Don't plan your retirement around inheritance — treat it as a bonus, not a certainty.
In-laws section
Same fields as parents — for your spouse's parents. Monthly support your spouse provides to in-laws is included in your household outflow. Their assets contribute to your spouse's inheritance share.
Spouse section
Enter spouse age, retirement age, and their own investments (EPF, MF, SIP, NPS, stocks). The tool runs a separate retirement projection for your spouse and shows adequacy in the Family Dashboard on the right.
💡 The Everyone's financial picture and all family data are included in the PDF report (Section 7) and Excel export (Sheet 6 — Family).
🎯 Goals Tab
Child yearly fees vs higher education
Annual fees: ongoing yearly school/college cost. Enter today's cost — the tool inflates at 8% p.a. (education inflation). Set "starts in X years" and "for Y years".
Higher education lump sum: one-time cost for IIT/IIM/MBBS/abroad in today's ₹. Enter separately.
School ₹1.5L/yr today → ₹3.1L/yr in 10 years at 8% inflation.
IIM MBA today ≈ ₹25–30L one-time.
Marriage / event corpus
Lump sum for child's wedding or other major event. Enter in today's ₹ — inflated to future value automatically. These are all deducted from your retirement corpus.
Loans — what to enter
Enter outstanding balance, monthly EMI, remaining tenure, and interest rate for up to 2 loans. Used to calculate how long EMIs reduce your investable surplus — and for the Prepay vs Invest calculator in the Tools tab.
One-time expenses
Any large one-time expense outside the above: home renovation, vehicle, foreign trip, gifting etc. Enter today's cost and when (in years).
🔧 Tools Tab
Prepay vs Invest
Enter your monthly surplus and the tool shows: if you prepay your home loan vs invest that surplus in equity — which gives you more wealth at the end of the loan tenure. Uses your actual loan data from the Goals tab.
SWP Simulator
Post-retirement withdrawal planning. Enter a monthly withdrawal amount — the tool shows exactly how long your corpus lasts under different return assumptions. Leave blank to use your calculated shortfall automatically.
Health Corpus Calculator
Shows how much corpus to set aside specifically for healthcare post-retirement, based on your current premium and medical inflation (typically 12–15% p.a. in India). Separate from your main retirement corpus.
Monte Carlo settings
The Monte Carlo simulation runs 1,000 scenarios with randomised annual returns. Change the return volatility slider to see how sensitive your plan is to market uncertainty. Results appear in the Monte Carlo card on the right panel.
Capital Gains Tax
Shows LTCG (12.5% above ₹1.25L) and STCG (20%) on your MF + stock holdings if you were to liquidate at retirement. Helps you plan if you're close to the LTCG threshold.
📊 Right Panel — Every Output Card Explained
⚡ Quick Start — shown in all modes
Can I retire? — verdict card
The very first card. Answers three questions in plain English: Do I have enough today? Will the corpus last my family lifetime? What should I change now?
If there is a shortfall it tells you exactly: "Increase monthly SIP by ₹X OR retire 2 years later OR reduce expenses by Y%." Shows in all three modes.
Readiness Score (0–100)
A single score across 6 dimensions: corpus adequacy, withdrawal rate, savings rate, emergency fund, diversification, and longevity coverage. 80+ = strong, 60–79 = on track, below 60 = action needed.
Hero numbers — corpus, net worth, family wealth
Three cards: Net corpus at retirement (financial assets only, after child goals and emergency fund), Personal net worth (includes gold, property), Family wealth pool (you + spouse + parents inheritance share).
Earliest retirement age / Safe monthly spend / Monthly surplus
Three quick metrics below the hero cards. Earliest age you can retire with current investments. Safe monthly spend in retirement — corpus-backed, inflation-adjusted. Monthly surplus available to invest today after all expenses and EMIs.
Investment Plan — what to do now
Pure calculation (no AI needed). Priority steps with exact rupee amounts: emergency fund top-up → term insurance → 80C/ELSS → NPS 80CCD(1B) → SIP increase → debt rebalancing. Tax savings shown in ₹/yr. Closes your retirement shortfall step by step.
📋 Full Plan (adds these)
Tax Regime Comparison — New vs Old
Computes your tax liability under both regimes using your CTC, 80C, 80D, HRA, and NPS deductions. Shows exact rupees saved per year and per month. Auto-highlights the better regime.
Do I have enough insurance?
Checks your term cover against the 12× annual income rule and your health cover against recommended amounts. Shows exact shortfall in rupees. Flags if policies end before retirement.
Will my money last?
Stacked bar chart from retirement to life expectancy. Green bars = pension + rental + spouse income. Purple bars = SWP drawn from corpus. Red dotted line = expenses growing with inflation. Shows exactly when corpus depletes (if it does) and warns: "Corpus depletes at age X — Y years short."
Can I retire earlier or later?
Three side-by-side cards showing retire 10 years early, 5 years early, and your plan. Each shows corpus, withdrawal rate, Monte Carlo success probability (200 quick runs), and how long money lasts. The best outcome gets a green badge.
How much can I spend each month?
Maximum monthly spend where corpus lasts exactly to life expectancy. Uses the inflation-adjusted PMT formula (not the crude 4% rule). Breaks down by source: SWP from corpus + pension + rental. Shows withdrawal rate and whether India-specific 3–3.5% safe rate is met.
Where will my income come from?
Breaks your post-retirement monthly income into sources: SWP from corpus, pension, rental income, NPS annuity, SCSS/PMVVY interest, spouse pension, part-time income. Each shows ₹/month and % of total. A final line says whether income covers expenses.
Am I saving enough for my children?
Shows inflation-adjusted corpus needed for each child: school fees (running cost × years), higher education (8% education inflation to target year), marriage. Total deducted from retirement corpus. Shows if you are on track to fund each goal.
How does my corpus grow year by year?
Shows how your corpus changes every year from today to life expectancy. Pre-retirement: how contributions and investment returns build the corpus. Post-retirement: how withdrawals draw it down. Transparent formula — you can verify every number. Every 5 years shown plus retirement year.
How much will I have at each age?
Milestone cards at Today, Retirement, +5yr, +10yr, +20yr showing corpus AND monthly expense at each age. Full detail table shows corpus, inflating monthly expenses, and draw from corpus (separate column showing what actually comes out vs what pension/rent covers). Green = healthy, amber = watch, red = depleted.
What if I change my SIP or retire later?
Drag to adjust retirement age, monthly SIP, or monthly expenses. See live corpus impact without changing your saved numbers. Range shown with min/max labels. Works on touch screens and mouse/trackpad.
How do I close the gap?
If there is a corpus shortfall, shows the exact gap in rupees and three ways to close it: increase SIP by ₹X/mo, delay retirement by Y years, or reduce expenses by Z%. Updates live as you change inputs.
Where is my money going?
Shows your gross corpus split by purpose: Retirement fund, Children goals (education + marriage, inflation-adjusted), Health buffer (10% for medical costs), Emergency fund, Available surplus. Horizontal bars with ₹ amount and percentage for each. Helps you see if you are over-indexing on one goal.
What will I be worth over time?
Allocation tab: Donut chart showing equity/debt/gold/real estate split with % and amount.
5-Year Milestones tab: Every instrument (EPF, PPF, MF, Stocks, RSU, Gold, Gratuity) projected at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 years and at retirement. YOUR TOTAL + Spouse row + YOU+SPOUSE combined.
Family Combined tab: Your wealth + spouse + parents inheritance + in-laws inheritance = FAMILY WEALTH POOL grand total at each milestone.
Will my parents need my support?
Year-by-year simulation of parents' corpus at 5-year intervals. Shows monthly income (pension), expenses (6% inflation), medical costs (12% inflation), corpus depletion. A "You need to fund" column appears when corpus is depleted. Red warning if money runs out before life expectancy.
My family picture, year by year
A table showing every 5-year milestone with all family members ages side by side — you, spouse, father, mother, in-laws. Also shows corpus, annual expenses, and status (Building / Retire / Drawing) at each year. Ages go yellow when retired, blank when beyond life expectancy.
🔧 Stress Test (adds these)
How likely is my plan to succeed?
Runs 1,000 random return scenarios using your inputs. Shows probability your corpus survives (e.g. 87% success). Histogram of outcomes across scenarios. 85%+ is considered robust. Best/worst/median outcome shown.
Full Family Snapshot
Adequacy grids for every family member — you, spouse, parents, in-laws. Shows corpus, monthly income, expenses, shortfall/surplus. Combined family corpus pool. Inheritance expected from parents and in-laws at their life expectancy.
What are my RSUs worth?
Full vesting schedule for up to 2 RSU grants. Post-tax value at each vest date (cliff + periodic). Countdown to next vest. Total unvested value. Corpus impact if all vested RSUs are invested at equity rate to retirement.
Is my portfolio balanced?
Compares your current equity/debt/gold split against the age-appropriate ideal allocation. Shows rebalancing moves in exact rupees: "Sell ₹X of debt funds, buy ₹X of equity MF." Updates as you age or change inputs.
How to draw income, reduce tax, and rebalance
SWP: Optimal monthly withdrawal amount, corpus survival years, growth vs draw-down chart.
CGT: LTCG with indexation on each asset class. Realised vs unrealised gains. Tax due on liquidation.
Glide Path: Equity-to-debt shift plan as you approach retirement. Year-wise rebalancing schedule.
Property sell & LTCG — liquidation toggle
Toggle "sell at retirement" on any property. The tool calculates future value at sell year, deducts LTCG tax (20% with indexation for pre-July 2024 properties, 12.5% without indexation for newer ones), then compounds the net proceeds to retirement. Automatically adds post-tax sale proceeds to your corpus. Shows in Full Plan and Stress Test.
Am I covered for medical costs?
Medical expenses modelled at 12%/yr inflation. Shows how much corpus to set aside for healthcare at age 70 and 80. Based on your health cover, premium, and family medical history inputs.
Should I prepay my loan? What if I retire in 10/20/30 yrs?
Prepay vs Invest: NPV comparison of home loan prepayment vs investing the lump sum at equity rate.
Horizon Comparison: Retire in 10 / 20 / 30 years side by side — corpus and survival.
Income Strategy: SCSS, PMVVY, POMIS allocation for guaranteed post-retirement income routing.
💾 Saving, Uploading & Exporting
💾 Save Data
Downloads a JSON file (e.g. RetireMitra_MyData_2025-01-15.json) to your computer with all 263 field values. Keep this file to restore your data in future sessions.
⬆ Upload / Restore
Select your previously saved JSON file. All 263 fields restore in under 2 seconds — exactly where you left off. Also accepts CSV (from the tool's own CSV export).
📋 Export PDF
Opens a professionally formatted report in a new browser window — dark themed, 9 sections: Executive Summary, Assumptions, Financial Assets, Cash Flow, Post-Retirement Timeline, Insurance, Family, Monte Carlo, Action Plan. To save as PDF: Ctrl+P (or Cmd+P) → Save as PDF.
📊 Export Excel
Downloads an 8-tab workbook: Summary, Financial Assets, Retirement Cash Flow, Corpus Timeline, Insurance, Family, Action Plan, All Inputs. Clean presentation format — share with your CA or family.
📄 Export CSV
All your data in a structured 3-column CSV (Field / Value / Unit). Opens in Excel, Google Sheets, or any spreadsheet tool.
Conservative / Base / Optimistic scenarios
Three different return assumptions — switch from the header bar. Base (12% equity, 6% inflation) is the default. Conservative (10% equity, 7% inflation) = stress test. Optimistic (15% equity, 5% inflation) = best case. Run all three to see your full range of outcomes.
✨ Features Guide
⚡ 📋 🔧 Three modes — Quick Start / Full Plan / Stress Test
Quick Start: 8 fields, 3 minutes, instant corpus and score.
Full Plan: 93 fields, 15 minutes — both incomes, family, goals, insurance, tax. The mode most people use.
Stress Test: 220+ fields, 30 minutes — Monte Carlo, RSU, CGT, SWP, glide path. For high-stakes decisions.
🔍 Field search (Ctrl+F)
Press Ctrl+F (or the search icon) to find any field instantly. Type "EPF", "PPF", "rental" — jumps directly to that field across any tab or section.
🎚️ What-if sliders
Drag sliders to adjust retirement age, SIP, or expenses and see live corpus impact — without changing your saved numbers. Available in Full Plan and Stress Test.
🔄 Liquidation toggles on every asset
Toggle any property, gold, or asset to "sell at retirement". Instantly see post-LTCG proceeds added to your corpus. Uncheck to exclude it. Works per-asset.
💡 Investment plan — what to invest and where
Calculated from your actual surplus and gaps. Priority steps with exact ₹ amounts: emergency fund → term insurance → 80C via ELSS → NPS 80CCD(1B) → SIP increase. Tax savings shown per step.
➕ Dynamic lists — unlimited FDs, policies, accounts
Add as many FDs, insurance policies, savings accounts, and endowment plans as you have. Each entry has its own fields. No artificial limits.
📋 Account & policy details (private)
Store UAN, PRAN, folio numbers, bank accounts, policy numbers alongside each investment. Saved in your JSON file — never sent anywhere. Useful as a family financial document.
🧪 Calculation test suite (Ctrl+Shift+T)
Press Ctrl+Shift+T or the 🧪 button in the nav bar to run 14 automated tests on the calculation engine. Each test checks a specific formula — EPF, PPF, SIP, bonus, loans, spouse corpus — against mathematically expected values. All tests run without touching the DOM.
⌨️ Number shorthand
Type 1L for ₹1,00,000 · 1Cr for ₹1,00,00,000 · 50k for ₹50,000. Converted automatically when you leave the field.
📊 Plan completeness meter
The progress bar at the top of the left panel shows how complete your plan is. More fields filled = more accurate results. Aim for 80%+ for the Full Plan mode.
🛡 Insurance adequacy check
Compares your term cover against the 12× annual income rule and health cover against family size. Shows exact shortfall in rupees. Flags if policies end before retirement.
⚠️ Input validation
Flags common errors: retirement age before current age, monthly expenses empty (critical — shows warning prominently), life expectancy too low. Warnings appear at the top of the right panel.
💾 Save, load and export
Save your plan as a JSON file and load it next session — all 220+ fields restored. Export as PDF (print-ready), Excel (all numbers in a spreadsheet), or CSV. The JSON is your master file — fill once, load forever.
📱 Mobile — Plan & Results tabs
On mobile, the bottom nav switches between Plan (inputs) and Results (outputs). The AI Advisor and Save buttons are always accessible. Touch-optimised sliders use Pointer Events API.
🌙 Light / dark mode
Follows your system preference automatically. Toggle manually via the sun/moon icon in the nav bar.
📱 Install as app (PWA)
On Chrome/Edge, click "Install" in the address bar to install Retire Mitra as a desktop or mobile app. Works offline. No app store needed.
